items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: Back with Louis, Roy, Roy Eldridge, he -- I remember the time when Dizzy used to sound a lot like Roy Eldridge.

ctx.x: And Dizzy certainly acknowledges the doors that preceded him.
Yes. Back with Louis, Roy, Roy Eldridge, he -- I remember the time when Dizzy used to sound a lot like Roy Eldridge.
Well, he admits this. He said that Roy was his inspiration.

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: like you take the people that I knew, like the Ellingtons, the Louis Armstrongs and all those kind of people

ctx.x: Of course we had a double side to it, because when the strike happened, all of the stars that later became stars, the singers, were just like side men in those days. Frank Sinatra, Dick Haymes. You know, they were just on the stand, because the band leaders ran the whole thing. And after the record industry found out that they could do without musicians, then the whole scene changed and the singers became stars. And then here comes -- oh, hi-fi, at that time. Then into stereo. So consequently you could get better…
